title: What Excel is for
summary: Workbooks, sheets and cells, and the real jobs that run on Excel.
objectives: Name the parts of a workbook: sheets, columns, rows, cells and ranges.
Read and write a cell address like **D4** and a range like **A1:E6**.
Say which everyday jobs Excel does well, and when another tool fits better.

slides.h: A workbook, its sheets and their cells
p: An Excel file is a **workbook**. Inside it are **worksheets**, and every worksheet is a grid of **cells**.
One workbook can hold many sheets: Orders, Customers, Notes.
Every sheet has the same grid of cells.
A cell holds text, a number, a date or a formula.
In real life: He keeps one workbook for the shop: a sheet for daily sales, one for stock and one for suppliers.

slides.h: Think of it like a notebook
p: If you have ever kept a ruled register, you already know how Excel is organised.
The big difference: Excel does the maths.
Change one number and every total that uses it updates.
In real life: Replaced its paper fee register with one workbook, one sheet per class. Totals that took an afternoon now take a second.

p: Columns are letters. Rows are numbers. Put them together and you get the cell's address.
Letter first, then number: **D4**, never 4D.
The **Name Box** above the grid shows the address of the cell you clicked.
After Z come AA, AB … a sheet has 16,384 columns and over a million rows.
In real life: says “check the amount in D4”. You find column D, go down to row 4, and you are looking at the same number.

lecture.title: Ranges, and what Excel is for

slides.h: A range is a block of cells
p: A **range** is a rectangle of cells, written as its first cell, a colon, and its last cell.
The colon means “from … to”.
Most Excel work happens on ranges: you format, sort and total them.
Dragging across cells selects a range.
In real life: She selects B2:B40, the salary column, and the bottom of the window shows the total payroll at once.

slides.h: The jobs that run on Excel
p: Any list where every row has the same details is an Excel job.
**Rows** are the things: orders, students, products.
**Columns** are the details about each: date, name, amount.
In real life: Prepares GST summaries for 40 clients in Excel: one row per invoice, with columns for date, amount and tax.

p: Simple test: is it a table of facts you will sort, count or calculate? Then use Excel.
Excel is not a word processor or a design tool.
Huge data shared by hundreds of people belongs in a database; Excel can read from it.
In real life: Wrote his project report in Excel. It looked messy and printed badly. In Word it took ten minutes.

demo.intro: Watch Sheetah move around a real workbook: single cells, a range, and another sheet.

steps.say: Click a cell to make it active. This is **A1**, the top-left corner.
Column D, row 4: cell **D4** holds Neha’s order amount. The Name Box at the top left always shows the active cell’s address.
Drag from A1 to E6 to select a **range**. Every order, every column.
Cell **D8** holds a formula. The grid shows its result; the formula bar shows `=SUM(D2:D6)`.
Sheet tabs at the bottom switch between worksheets. This is the **Customers** sheet.

demo.outro: Cells, ranges and sheets: that’s the whole map. Now you find your way around.

lab.intro: Explore the shop’s workbook. Click cells, select a range, switch sheets and rename one.

tasks.prompt: Click cell **C5** to make it active.
hints: The column letter comes first: find column C.
Click the cell where column C meets row 5. The Name Box should say C5.
tasks.explain: C5 is Lucknow, Imran Khan’s city.

tasks.prompt: What is in cell **B3** on the Orders sheet?
hints: It’s the customer of order SH-1042.
tasks.explain: B3 is the Customer column, row 3.

tasks.prompt: Select the range **A1:E6**: all the orders with their headers.
hints: Then hold Shift and click E6.
Or drag from A1 down to E6. The status bar shows Count: 30.

tasks.prompt: Cell D8 shows 14,260. What is really inside it?
hints: Look at the formula bar, not the cell.
The bar shows what was typed: a formula.
tasks.explain: The cell shows the result; the formula bar shows the formula that makes it.
options: Text that looks like a number

tasks.prompt: Rename the sheet **Notes** to **Ideas**. Double-click its tab, type the new name and press Enter.
hints: The tabs are at the bottom of the grid.
Type Ideas in the box that appears and press Enter.
tasks.explain: Clear sheet names make big workbooks easy to find your way around.

quiz.explain: The file is the workbook; the grids inside are worksheets.

quiz.q: Where do you see the formula inside a cell?
quiz.explain: The cell shows the result; the formula bar shows the formula.

quiz.q: Which job is Excel the wrong tool for?
quiz.explain: Long documents belong in Word; Excel is for tables of facts you calculate with.

points: A **workbook** holds **worksheets**; each sheet is a grid of **cells**.
A cell address is column then row: **D4**. A range is first:last: **A1:E6**.
Excel fits any table of facts you want to sort, count or calculate.
recap.cheat: Column letter, then row number: D4. Two cells and a colon make a range: A1:E6.
